es.summary: Proceso por el cual el organismo transforma los fármacos en compuestos más fáciles de eliminar, principalmente en el hígado mediante enzimas del citocromo P450.
key_points: El metabolismo ocurre en dos fases: reacción de biotransformación (fase I) y conjugación (fase II).
El efecto de primer paso (first‑pass) reduce la biodisponibilidad de los fármacos orales.
Factores que alteran el metabolismo: edad, función hepática, genética, interacciones con inhibidores o inductores enzimáticos.
Metabolitos pueden ser activos, inactivos o tóxicos.
La monitorización de niveles plasmáticos es esencial para fármacos con estrecho margen terapéutico.

mechanism: Fase I: oxidación, reducción o hidrólisis mediante enzimas CYP450, generando metabolitos más polares.
Fase II: conjugación con glucurónido, sulfato, glutatión, aumentando la solubilidad en agua.
Primer paso hepático elimina gran parte del fármaco antes de llegar a la circulación sistémica.
Metabolitos pueden ser excretados por riñón o bilis.
nursing_care: Evaluar función hepática (AST, ALT, bilirrubina) antes de iniciar fármacos de amplio metabolismo.
Obtener niveles séricos del fármaco cuando exista margen terapéutico estrecho.
Ajustar dosis si el paciente presenta insuficiencia hepática o está tomando inhibidores/inductores CYP.
Observar signos de toxicidad (náuseas, ictericia, alteración del estado mental).
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si los niveles plasmáticos superan el rango terapéutico.
patient_teaching: Informar que el consumo de alcohol o jugo de pomelo puede alterar el metabolismo de algunos fármacos.
Explicar la importancia de no suspender el medicamento sin consultar al profesional de salud.
Recomendar reportar cualquier cambio inesperado en la salud, como ictericia o fatiga.
Indicar que la adherencia al horario de dosis ayuda a mantener niveles plasmáticos estables.

related_to: uso concomitante de inhibidores o inductores enzimáticos
outcomes: Riesgo de intoxicación disminuido: paciente sin signos de toxicidad al alta
Niveles plasmáticos del fármaco dentro del rango terapéutico en 48 h

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar pruebas de función hepática (AST, ALT, bilirrubina) antes de iniciar el fármaco
interventions.rationale: Detectar alteraciones que puedan disminuir la capacidad de metabolizar el medicamento

interventions.action: Monitorear niveles séricos del fármaco según indicación del médico
interventions.rationale: Asegurar que la concentración permanezca dentro del rango terapéutico

interventions.action: Revisar la lista de medicamentos para identificar inhibidores o inductores del CYP450
interventions.rationale: Prevenir interacciones que alteren la velocidad de metabolismo

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre alimentos y bebidas que pueden afectar el metabolismo (ej. jugo de pomelo, alcohol)
interventions.rationale: Reducir factores externos que modifiquen la biotransformación del fármaco

interventions.action: Ajustar la dosis o intervalo de administración según resultados de pruebas y respuesta clínica
interventions.rationale: Optimizar la terapia y minimizar el riesgo de toxicidad

en.summary: Process by which the body transforms drugs into compounds that are easier to eliminate, primarily in the liver via cytochrome P450 enzymes.
key_points: Metabolism occurs in two phases: biotransformation reaction (Phase I) and conjugation (Phase II).
The first‑pass effect reduces the oral bioavailability of drugs.
Factors that alter metabolism: age, hepatic function, genetics, interactions with enzyme inhibitors or inducers.
Metabolites may be active, inactive, or toxic.
Monitoring plasma levels is essential for drugs with a narrow therapeutic index.

mechanism: Phase I: oxidation, reduction, or hydrolysis by CYP450 enzymes, generating more polar metabolites.
Phase II: conjugation with glucuronic acid, sulfate, glutathione, increasing water solubility.
First‑pass hepatic metabolism removes a large portion of the drug before it reaches systemic circulation.
Metabolites can be excreted by kidney or bile.
nursing_care: Assess hepatic function (AST, ALT, bilirubin) before initiating drugs with extensive metabolism.
Obtain serum drug levels when a narrow therapeutic index exists.
Adjust dose if the patient has hepatic insufficiency or is taking CYP inhibitors/inducers.
Observe for signs of toxicity (nausea, jaundice, altered mental status).
Withhold the dose and notify the physician if plasma levels exceed the therapeutic range.
patient_teaching: Inform that alcohol or grapefruit juice can alter the metabolism of certain drugs.
Explain the importance of not discontinuing medication without consulting a health professional.
Recommend reporting any unexpected health changes, such as jaundice or fatigue.
Indicate that adherence to dosing schedule helps maintain stable plasma levels.

related_to: concomitant use of CYP inhibitors or inducers
outcomes: Risk for poisoning decreased: patient without signs of toxicity at discharge
Drug plasma levels within therapeutic range within 48 h

interventions.action: Obtain and record hepatic function tests (AST, ALT, bilirubin) before starting the drug
interventions.rationale: Detect alterations that may reduce the ability to metabolize the medication

interventions.action: Monitor serum drug levels as ordered by the physician
interventions.rationale: Ensure concentration remains within therapeutic range

interventions.action: Review medication list to identify CYP450 inhibitors or inducers
interventions.rationale: Prevent interactions that alter metabolism rate

interventions.action: Educate patient about foods and beverages that may affect metabolism (e.g., grapefruit juice, alcohol)
interventions.rationale: Reduce external factors that modify drug biotransformation

interventions.action: Adjust dose or dosing interval based on test results and clinical response
interventions.rationale: Optimize therapy and minimize toxicity risk

key_points.1.quote: The first-pass effect can potentially decrease the bioavailability of a drug significantly.

key_points.4.quote: Drug monitoring is sometimes required for drugs with a narrow therapeutic window to ensure that the client’s drug level stays within a safe range.

sections.mechanism.2.quote: After absorption, oral drugs can also be metabolized in the liver before entering systemic circulation, a process called first-pass metabolism.

sections.mechanism.3.quote: Although the removal of a drug occurs primarily through the renal system, it may also occur through the lungs, skin, bile, or feces.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Drug monitoring is sometimes required for drugs with a narrow therapeutic window to ensure that the client’s drug level stays within a safe range.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Drug concentrations can also accumulate if drug-metabolizing organs are not functioning properly and the dose is not adjusted accordingly.
